text:
Samira (design): quick design review — putting the canary split control inline with the version chips feels cramped on narrow screen. thoughts?
Jon L: I noticed that too. on mobile the percentage input wraps awkwardly. maybe move percentage into a popover? :thinking_face:
Asha: popover could work but we lose visibility of allocation during quick scans. want to keep a one-line glance.
Matt D: what if we collapse to a compact pill that shows "Canary 5%" and tapping expands to slider + exact input. keeps glanceability + access to precise control.
Samira (design): like a micro-accordion. love it. accessibility check: ensure expand/collapse is keyboard focusable and announces state to screen readers.
Evan: noted — aria-expanded on the pill and role=button, plus an offscreen label that reads current allocation should do it. we should also trap focus into the expanded panel while it's open.
Asha: trap focus is important. also add a confirm/save action in the expanded view instead of auto-save on slider — prevents accidental allocation flips during a quick tap.
Jon L: agree on explicit save. UX copy nits: current label "canary" is ambiguous for non-technical PMs. propose "Staged rollout" for main label and leave a tooltip that says "aka canary / A/B".
Samira (design): good call. shorter primary label + help text. update copy: primary="Staged rollout" secondary="Start small, increase over time" tooltip="Canary / A/B test"
Matt D: small visual nudge — when you hover the version timeline, show a subtle dotted outline for the version under pointer and expose a quick "rollback" icon in the corner. needs keyboard equivalent.
Evan: keyboard equivalent could be focusing the version and having a contextual menu via kebab with "Rollback to this version". Also ensure rollback requires two-step confirmation: reason + checkbox "I understand impact" for auditability.
Asha: can we make the confirmation copy less scary? current modal says "This will revert production" — propose: "Revert traffic to this version. This will not delete data but may change live behavior." Small but clearer.
Samira (design): love clearer language. also accessibility: the confirmation modal should shift focus to the first input (reason) and return focus to the version chip after close.
Jon L: perf question — hovering timeline currently triggers a network call for metrics. that makes hover laggy. can we debounce or prefetch metrics on timeline entry?
Evan: implement local caching + 300ms debounce. for small teams we can always show cached sparkline and lazy-load detailed metrics in the expanded panel.
deploy-bot: deploy-preview for "staged-rollout-ux-v3" is available at https://console.redwood.ai/preview/ux/staged-rollout-3 :white_check_mark:
Samira (design): thanks deploy-bot. i'll attach new mockups (compact pill + expanded slider + rollback modal copy) to the Figma thread.
Asha: one last nit — color contrast on the 5% badge is borderline. increase contrast and add an icon-only focus ring.
Matt D: will update CSS: color and focus outline. snippet I'll use: ```css .version-pill:focus { outline: 3px solid #0a66ff; } .alloc-badge { color: #0f1724; background:#fff9c4; } ```
Samira (design): perfect. next steps: Matt to patch CSS + keyboard menu, Evan to add aria attributes + debounce, Jon to update copy in content repo, Asha to validate confirmation tone. I'll re-run accessibility pass after patches. :raised_hands:
Evan: on it. planning to include unit tests for focus order and a11y smoke tests.
Jon L: i'll PR the copy updates today.
Asha: scheduling a short sync if needed but otherwise i'll sign off after the accessibility pass.
Samira (design): thanks all — aiming for rollout in next sprint. :rocket:
